sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) including Investment Chapter
Panama-European Union Free Trade Agreement (provisionally applied)
Panama-South Korea Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of April 27, 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Law 70 of October 22, 2019 and regulated by Executive Decree No. 406 of November 30, 2019; Private Interest Foundation Law (Law 25 of June 12, 1995, as amended by Law 41 of 2017)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Paz y Salvo) of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público / corporate registry of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague signatory countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport bio-page of each founder, council member and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport issuance authority (or notary public of the country of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of physical address (or utility bill) for each UBO, council member and resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local municipal authority or utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or legalized as required for due diligence file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Institutional Power of Attorney for the incorporator/resident agent (if filing through counsel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All stakeholders (founder, council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficial owners) undergo mandatory screening against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (ii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, (iii) the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and (iv) Panama's list of persons linked to money laundering published by the Public Registry/Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF). Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), persons from high-risk jurisdictions per FATF, and governmental or multilateral organization representatives; screening results must be documented in a compliance file retained for at least five years under Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — en línea (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be submitted in Spanish or in a Latin-script transliteration; if it includes a foreign language word, a Spanish transcription must be provided. The name must contain a distinctive denomination followed by the expression 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'FIP'. Names must not be identical or phonetically equivalent to any existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is appealable by means of a 'recurso de reconsideración' filed with the Directorship General of the Public Registry within five business days of rejection notice, followed by an administrative appeal ('recurso de apelación') before the higher registry tribunal within ten business days; if exhausted, judicial review may be sought before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Supreme Court of Justice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the registered office so long as a licensed resident agent maintains a physical address in the Republic of Panama for service of legal process; no local physical business premises are required for a non-operating PIF. If the foundation engages in payroll-processing activities within Panama, a physical commercial establishment would become subject to municipal operating license and workplace compliance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a non-operating PIF holding intangible assets outside Panama, probability of an unannounced physical inspection is low (<5% per year); risk increases to approximately 25% if a physical office is located in Panama or if the foundation is flagged in AML/CFT risk profiling.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Resident Agent (Abogado de Libre Ejercicio)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of foundation charter and regulations (Spanish text)
Initial inscription fee before the Public Registry
UBO information filing and AML/KYC compilation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama or Panamanian Consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of June 12, 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Arts. 1-40), as amended by Law No. 41 of 2007, and applicable Public Registry regulations; supplemental application of the general commercial and civil rules of the Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundations Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under Law No. 25 of 1995; the Founder must designate initial assets sufficient for the Foundation's lawful purpose (market standard: at least US$10,000.00). No government escrow or depositary account is required; assets may be contributed in cash, securities, or in-kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The Founder subscribes the initial endowment of the Foundation in the amount of Ten Thousand United States Dollars (US$10,000.00), constituting the Foundation assets under Law No. 25 of 1995. RESOLVED SECOND: The registered office of the Foundation is established at the office of the Resident Agent in the City of Panama, Republic of Panama. RESOLVED THIRD: The undersigned Foundation Council members are appointed, and the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are elected, with full power to open bank accounts, execute contracts, engage staff, and administer the payroll automation software business. RESOLVED FOURTH: The Council is authorized to adopt the Bylaws within the statutory one-year period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foundation Name Verification and Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Name Search Service (Buscada de Nombre / Certificado de Denominaciones Sociales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Panamanian resident agent submits a written name request, either online or at the Registry's Mercantile Section counter. The Registry verifies the requested denomination against active registered legal entities, including foundations and corporations. The search is executed and the availability certificate is issued on the same day; the agent then uses the certificate to draft the Foundation Charter.
required_dossiers: Written name-search application identifying the proposed payroll SaaS foundation denomination
Passport copy of the Founder (or certificate of good standing if the Founder is a corporate entity)
Executed resident-agency engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is rejected as conflicting or confusingly similar, the agent re-submits up to three alternative names and pays the statutory re-search fee; the clean availability certificate is then used for charter drafting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder executes the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary, either in person or through a duly appointed attorney-in-fact. The charter states the foundation's name, purpose (including ISIC 6201 payroll automation and staff compliance software activities), initial assets, registered office, resident agent appointment, and transfer rules. The instrument remains a private document; no publication in the Official Gazette is required for private interest foundations.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) in Spanish, executed in duplicate
Valid passport of the Founder or authenticated power of attorney
Acceptance letter of the Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney)
Proof of initial endowment (bank reference or asset declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary identify formal irregularities, the charter is re-executed and re-signed by the parties before filing; no financial penalty is applied if correction occurs prior to Registry presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Filing at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent presents the notarized Foundation Charter, the covering sheet (foja de presentación), and the government fee receipt. The Registry assigns a running entry and, upon approval, inscribes the Foundation, granting separate juridical personality and patrimony separation. The registration record and inscription status are tracked electronically.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter with notarial seals
Payment voucher for the statutory Registry fee (US$250.00)
Resident Agent appointment certificate (Certificado de Agente Residente)
Cover letter/index sheet signed by the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a Nota de Observación or requires supplements, the agent has 15 business days to cure the defect by reforming the instrument and paying the minor annotation fee; a rejected filing may be re-presented with corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Foundation Certificate and Registered File Excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Records and Certification Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registered, the Registry issues the Foundation Certificate (Ficha de Fundación) recording the inscription number and date. The resident agent obtains certified copies of the registered deed and the certificate, which serve as proof of legal existence for banking, tax, and commercial counterparty purposes.
required_dossiers: Registration filing receipt (provided at Step 3)
Payment certificate of certified-copy fees
Written request for certified copies (if requested remotely)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, the agent files a written expedited request or obtains a temporary Registry certification (Certificado Provisional) to proceed with tax and banking procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC) with the National Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenues (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent registers the Foundation in the RUC system via the DGI portal (SIRI), identifying the Foundation as an employer and a taxpayer. Because the Foundation will operate a payroll SaaS platform, it obtains full RUC status, territorial-tax classification, fiscal address, and employer registration. Foreign-source revenues are outside Panamanian income tax under the territorial model.
required_dossiers: Foundation Certificate (Ficha) and registered charter excerpt
RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
Resident Agent certificate of fiscal domicile (Acreditación de Sede Fiscal)
Authenticated power of attorney for the DGI representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI electronic form is flagged or rejected, the agent corrects the validation errors and re-submits with the certified Foundation Certificate; for substantive classification doubts, the agent files a written petition confirming territorial taxation of non-Panamanian source payroll revenue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Operating Notice and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) – Business Notice Directorate; licensed commercial banks subject to Decree Law No. 2 of 2008 (AML) for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Foundation files the Aviso de Operación to obtain the municipal operating permit for its registered office. Concurrently, the Foundation opens corporate USD bank accounts with ACH and SWIFT wire capabilities by submitting the formation certificate, RUC credential, founding resolutions, and AML/client-onboarding documents. The endorsed Aviso de Operación constitutes the local operating license for the software services scope.
required_dossiers: RUC registration certificate (DGI)
Foundation Certificate and notarized charter excerpt
Lease agreement or property title of the Panamanian registered office
AML/KYC forms, proof of source of funds, and corporate operating resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality issues a deficiency notice, the agent supplements the application within 10 days (zoning or site plan); if the bank requires enhanced due diligence for a medium-risk payroll software activity, the client provides a business plan, client contracts, and a sworn source-of-funds declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias – MICI); no industrial manufacturing license applies to ISIC 6201 software services; local operation is governed by the Municipality of Panama Business Notice regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación – Municipal Business Notice (category: computer programming and software development services, ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541214)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – No Environmental Impact Study required for office-based digital services under Executive Decree No. 123 of 2009; an environmental registration declaration (Declaración Jurada de Cumplimiento Ambiental) is sufficient for the physical office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge streams; office wastewater routed to municipal sewers in compliance with Administrative Resolution No. 336 of 1998 (discharge parameters: BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L); no point-source VOC emissions; e-waste (servers, monitors, IT peripherals) must be transferred to authorized recyclers under Law No. 55 of 2012; energy-efficiency reporting under Law No. 67 of 2011 when applicable thresholds are met.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SINAPROC Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (Certificado de Inspección de Seguridad Humana) required before office occupancy; municipal structural and load-use clearance (Permiso de Uso de Local) issued by the Municipality of Panama; workplace registration with the Social Security Fund (Caja de Seguro Social – CSS) and occupational health and safety compliance under MITRADEL regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), República de Panamá. Centralized e-services portal: 'Sede Electrónica de la DGI' at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa; institutional site: https://www.dgi.gob.pa. RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) administration, ITBMS registration, e-invoicing validation, and annual declarations are all processed through this authority, with interoperability with the Registro Público de Panamá and the Servicio Nacional de Aduanas.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its RUC as follows: (1) register the PIF with the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed resident agent (abogado idóneo) and file the foundation's Aviso de Operación / business notice with the DGI; (2) have the resident agent activate the DGI digital identity (Firma Digital issued by a Registro Público-authorized certifier) and open the 'Sede Electrónica' account; (3) submit the RUC application electronically, attaching the public-registry certificate, foundation charter (acta de dotación and estatutos), identification of the foundation council and founder, and the registered Panamanian address; (4) upon issuance of the RUC, opt into ITBMS and e-invoicing modules to obtain the taxpayer's e-filing credentials and invoice emission codes. Non-resident principals do not file personally; their authority is exercised through the resident agent. The RUC certificate is delivered digitally and must be kept current for the annual PIF tax return and 'Paz y Salvo' clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not have a check-the-box or S-corporation-style election. A PIF is conclusively treated for tax purposes as a territorial asset-holding legal person: income sourced outside Panama (e.g., the payroll SaaS subscription/licensing fees of non-resident clients) is exempt from Panamanian income tax, while Panama-sourced income is taxable at the 25% corporate rate. The PIF may elect voluntarily to register as an ITBMS taxpayer in order to zero-rate its export services; it may also elect the simplified small-taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) ITBMS settlement where gross receipts are within the applicable threshold. No fiscal-transparency or hybrid-mismatch election is available; the PIF is itself the taxpayer. Regardless of elections, the PIF must pay the fixed annual foundation tax of B/.300.00 and file the annual declaration (declaración jurada) to maintain good standing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panama's VAT-type consumption tax established by Ley 55 de 2008 and administered under the Código Fiscal by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis exemption: any person habitually making taxable supplies in Panama (including cross-border digital services used or enjoyed in Panama) must register for ITBMS from the first taxable supply. A small-taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) presumptive/simplified régime applies under DGI rules for annual gross turnover up to approximately B/.36,000. Non-resident digital suppliers have a zero threshold and register through the simplified remote procedure if their services are effectively used in Panamanian territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a mandatory DGI electronic-invoicing regime (Resolución DGI No. 201-5144 of 2021, as amended) phased in by taxpayer category from 2022. All ITBMS-registered businesses must issue invoices exclusively through DGI-certified software and transmit each invoice to the DGI 'Facturación Electrónica' platform for real-time validation, receiving an acceptance code and QR verification stamp before legal issuance to the customer; offline/contingency emission requires immediate post-facto upload. VAT and export invoices must quote the taxpayer's RUC and pre-registered emission point. Export e-invoices must reference the customs export declaration and are machine-cross-checked with customs data. Non-resident digital-service suppliers use the simplified remote registration and invoice-emission protocol.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports are eligible for 0% ITBMS under Ley 55 de 2008 and DGI guidance when (a) goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory, or (b) services are performed for a non-resident client and used/exploited wholly outside Panama. The payroll automation platform qualifies where the SaaS subscription, data processing, and HR compliance services are supplied to a foreign employer/payroll beneficiary with no Panamanian permanent establishment, are paid in foreign currency from abroad, and produce no benefit or economic use within Panama. Incidental back-office activity in Panama does not defeat zero-rating if the recipient and place of effective use remain offshore. Services used in Panama, or rendered to a Panamanian-resident entity, are subject to 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed through Panama's Single Window / Servicio Nacional de Aduanas module, containing the DGI cross-reference and ITBMS export-regime code
DGI e-invoicing export invoice (Factura Electrónica de Exportación) bearing the validated acceptance code and export specification
Commercial invoice / sales contract and, for goods, Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB); for services, the signed service agreement, delivery/access certificates, and platform usage evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank credit advice demonstrating repatriation of export proceeds into Panama within the statutory deadline

Supporting due-diligence file: non-resident client's foreign tax ID/registration, beneficial-ownership data, IPR license records, and GL/HR-payroll records evidencing the offshore place of performance and use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits export zero-rating through automated cross-checks of the customs e-export declaration, the validated export e-invoice, and the banking FX-inflow record within the 180-day repatriation window. Missing or inconsistent documentation converts the export into an ordinary taxable supply, triggering retroactive ITBMS at 7%, default interest, surcharges, and denial/recapture of refunds. Knowingly false declarations, forged transport documents, fake invoices, or non-repatriated proceeds constitute tax fraud (defraudación fiscal): fines of 100%–300% of the evaded tax, cancellation of export registration and RUC good standing, clawback of any refund with statutory interest, and criminal liability including imprisonment for aggravated evasion for the foundation, its council members, and complicit resident agents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — acting as the official banking supervisory authority under the absence of a central bank; monetary policy and currency issuance are functionally delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve System through full dollarization
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with the U.S. dollar as sole legal tender; there are no exchange controls, no capital account restrictions, and no distinction between current and capital account convertibility. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted though may be subject to source-of-funds and AML documentation. Legal entity taxation follows a territorial system; corporate and foundation income is taxable only on Panamanian-source income. The absence of a central bank means no foreign exchange parity risk exists for USD-denominated treasury operations, and FX conversion to other currencies is performed by commercial banks at freely negotiated market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama does not impose any mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion timeline for export proceeds. Exporters and service providers, including payroll SaaS platforms, may hold, invoice, and disburse export receipts in USD or any convertible currency without statutory holding ratios, minimum conversion obligations, or release requirements under Central Bank decrees.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Panama does not maintain a statutory electronic money institution (EMI) licence comparable to the EU/UK EMI regime. A cross-border digital bank or EMI can only operate by obtaining a full banking licence under the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, by partnering with a cloud-banking platform with an existing Panamanian bank licence, or by functioning through an offshore entity subject to unregulated-status review by domestic banks. The PIF may lawfully hold accounts at a Panamanian bank, but onboarding of money held through non-bank offshore EMI rails is severely constrained by AML/CFT anti-shelling rules, KYC documentation requirements, and the high risk of account closure if the EMI has no physical presence or regulatory registration in a recognized reciprocal jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is presumed mandatory. In practice, Tier-1 Panamanian commercial banks require the beneficial owner or at least one director and the resident agent or a board-approved legal representative with a notarized and apostilled power-of-attorney to attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank’s Panama branch. Remote opening is technically allowable only for low-risk corporate clients under the bank’s enhanced due diligence framework, and even then requires a pre-recorded video interview, certified true-copy documents, and a notarized verification by the registered agent. For PIF and offshore structures relying on nominee directors, full physical appearance of all parties evidencing source of funds and business activity is strongly recommended if onboarding is to be approved at high confidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF formed under foreign foundations law without visible economic activity; nominee director or protector absent in Panama; source of funds comprises cryptocurrency exchange transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or apostilled Foundation Charter and notarized Regulations; valid Registered Agent License and certified Registered Agent Certificate; notarized Certificate of Good Standing issued by the PIF Registry; complete source-of-wealth declaration with supporting bank references for the founding contributors; corporate and foundation annual return filings evidencing initial capital; sworn declaration of beneficial ownership; audited or certified financials of the payroll SaaS operating entity; and a legal opinion letter from a Panamanian law firm describing the foundation’s purpose and absence of per se tax-secrecy intention.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll SaaS platform has zero local operational footprint in Panama, provides cross-border payroll services, and maintains higher-than-average transaction volumes during month-end payroll cycles; underwriting models may identify potential unauthorized money service business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed SaaS contract template and client list; platform service agreements showing fixed software subscription and payroll-processing fees rather than money transmission; employment verification documents of internal staff; evidence of IT infrastructure and server outsourcing; audited financial statements matching transaction velocity; written compliance policy for employee and client screening; and a tailored tax-analysis opinion confirming territorial taxation and non-licensing-risk under Panamanian law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the shareholder or contributor’s bank to the PIF’s Panamanian bank account using the purpose code
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for payroll and vendor disbursements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for uncomplicated wire transfers and through Commercial Letters of Credit (Documentary Import/Export LC) where supplier contracts require guaranteed settlement. [[Panama's local payments system, known as ACH Directo, permitssame-day domestic clearing in USD, while international payments rely on correspondent banking relationships with U.S. and European clearing banks. All outbound transactions require underlying commercial invoices or contractual documentation to substantiate cross-border transfers and comply with the bank's internal AML/EDD policies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (DNDF prohibited or unnecessary due to USD legal tender status; deliverable forwards can cover EUR, GBP, or MXN settlement needs)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única de Fundación) — government renewal tax for the Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 of each calendar year (first quarter); no statutory extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax; non-payment for two consecutive annual periods authorizes the Registro Público to initiate administrative strike-off or suspension of the foundation's legal standing, including loss of good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Register Confirmation (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales) — annual UBO register update and confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year registrants); any change in shareholding or foundation council membership must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or deliberate omission attracts administrative fines up to B/.10,000 (USD 10,000), suspension of the foundation's registry privileges, and blocking of solvency certificates; unregistered ownership changes are treated as ineffective vis-à-vis third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) — territorial-source income tax return for the foundation's Panamanian-source revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and under-declaration penalties range from B/.100 up to B/.2,500, plus monthly interest of 1%; material omissions may be penalized with 10% of the omitted tax due and can trigger an official tax audit and administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Submission (Estado Financiero Anual) — financial statements to accompany the annual tax return and satisfy audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the income tax return (March 31 for calendar-year); for entities exceeding the audit threshold, the audited financial statements must be available and accepted by the DGI at filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-Submission or rejection of financial statements can produce a tax penalty of up to B/.10,000 plus interest, loss of tax-payment credentials, and enhanced scrutiny; repeated failures may lead to administrative penalty proceedings before the Tribunal Administrativo Tributario.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to: (i) any legal person whose gross annual income exceeds B/.1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000); (ii) entities regulated by the Superintendency of Banks, Superintendency of Insurance, or Superintendency of Securities Market; (iii) entities listed on the Panama Stock Exchange; and (iv) foundations engaging in financial intermediation, trust, or collective investment activities. Foundations below these thresholds may file unaudited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama (NIIF) for regulated and public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) is permitted for unregulated small and medium entities. Tax returns are reconciled to Panamanian Código Fiscal rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 52 of 2016 and the AML Rulebook, the Private Interest Foundation must maintain a current final beneficial owner register with qualified identification, residential address, tax ID, and percentages of economic interest. Any shareholding or foundation council membership transfer must be recorded internally within 30 days and reflected in the annual UBO confirmation filed with the DGI. The annual confirmation is mandatory even when no changes occurred; failure to file for two consecutive years results in suspension of the foundation's operational registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (if any) and Beneficial Owners
Register of Directors and Foundation Council Members

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat headline rate on Panamanian-source net taxable income above USD 50,000, preceded by a progressive bracket scale: 15% on the first USD 11,000 of taxable income and 20% on taxable income between USD 11,001 and USD 50,000 (Article 699-A, Código Fiscal, as amended by Law 8 of 2010 and subsequent reforms). Foreign-source income remains outside the territorial tax base for a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) whose commercial activity is executed abroad.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial sourcing relief: the PIF's income from automated payroll SaaS licensing to non-Panamanian clients (ISIC 6201) is excluded from the ISR base when the services are rendered abroad and no Panamanian-source revenue stream exists. Export of digital services is also outside the ITBMS (VAT) scope. The PIF is subject only to a flat annual franchise contribution of USD 300 paid by 15 January. A 15% Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax applies from fiscal year 2025 onward only to multinational groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million under Law 365 of 2024; a standalone PIF is not in scope unless part of such a group.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 026 – Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas, filed exclusively through the DGI E-tax 2.0 electronic portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas). The PIF must first obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and file an Aviso de Operación prior to rendering software services.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return, accompanied by 12 monthly advance payments (Pagos Directos / Anticipos) during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form 026 is due no later than three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year PIF, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. Monthly advance payments of ISR are due on the 15th day of each month. The USD 300 annual foundation tax is due by 15 January of each year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (RUC), Digital Verification code (DV), legal name of the Private Interest Foundation, fiscal period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the PIF by its foundation number issued under Law 25 of 1995 and the RUC; the resident agent's data must match the registered public registry record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC Rev.4 code of the main activity and a brief description of the business (automated payroll SaaS platform).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 6201; do not reference the foreign parent's activity. The activity description must evidence real economic operations rather than passive asset holding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 05 – Gross Revenue from Panamanian Source
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts derived from services rendered, licenses, or software subscriptions consumed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF serving only foreign clients, this box should be zero or de minimis; every dollar claimed as foreign-source must be substantiated by contracts, bank statements, and client invoices showing delivery abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue excluded from the territorial tax base, including export SaaS income contractually performed and consumed outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed schedule of foreign-source revenue by jurisdiction, supporting invoices, IP licensing agreements, and evidence of server/delivery location. This is the highest-risk box in a DGI audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to delivering the SaaS platform (hosting, third-party software components, subcontractor costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure cost allocations follow arm's length principles and are supported by intercompany agreements and transfer pricing documentation when the counterparty is related.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operational expenses: salaries of foundation staff, legal fees, resident agent fees, accounting fees, IT infrastructure, marketing, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be documented and correspond to actual economic substance in Panama; expenses that are not adequately documented are automatically disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source revenue minus deductible costs and expenses, adjusted for non-deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Box 05 is zero, Box 13 should normally be zero or negative; inconsistent positive income with no Panamanian activity triggers immediate audit flags.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 – ISR Computed at Applicable Scale
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated applying the 15% / 20% / 25% progressive brackets to the net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify no foreign-source income is erroneously included; compute the brackets strictly on the Panamanian-source base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 – Credit for Monthly Advance Payments (Anticipos)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of the 12 monthly advance ISR payments made during the fiscal year, credited against the annual tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile E-tax payment receipts; discrepancies trigger automatic notices and surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net ISR payable after deduction of advances, or the amount to be carried forward as a credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any balance via the E-tax portal by the statutory deadline; no payment reminders are issued.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on dividends or profit distributions made to foundation beneficiaries from Panamanian-source taxable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions from foreign-source exempt profits are not subject to this box; document the source of each distribution to avoid double characterization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 026: fine ranging from USD 50 to USD 5,000 plus a 10% surcharge on the tax due; late payment accrues monthly interest of 1% on the unpaid balance. Persistent non-filing triggers official determination by DGI (determinación de oficio), suspension of the Aviso de Operación, and seizure of bank accounts. The USD 300 annual foundation tax, if unpaid by 15 January, accumulates fines of USD 20 per month (capped) and may block issuance of the Paz y Salvo fiscal certificate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Panama PIF out of profits that were subject to Panamanian ISR (Article 733, Código Fiscal). Distributions funded exclusively from exempt foreign-source income are not subject to the 10% dividend tax, but the burden of proof lies on the PIF to trace distributable reserves to non-Panamanian sources.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a Panama income tax treaty (e.g., United States, United Kingdom, Netherlands, Singapore, Mexico, France, Luxembourg, Spain, Italy, South Korea), the recipient must (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the tax authority of its residence country; (2) submit the certificate, a beneficial owner declaration, and the treaty relief application to the Panamanian withholding agent before the payment date; (3) complete the DGI's 'Solicitud de Aplicación de Convenio' procedure. The withholding agent must retain the documentation for five years; filing after the payment date generally forfeits the relief for that distribution. Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clauses and the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the BEPS MLI apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical assistance fees paid by a Panamanian PIF for the use of trademarks, patents, software copyrights, or know-how in Panama are subject to 12.5% statutory withholding on the gross Panamanian-source payment. Treaty-protected rates typically range from 5% to 10% (e.g., 10% under the US-Panama DTA, 5%-10% under several EU treaties) subject to full-benefit entitlement. Interest paid to a non-resident lender on debts secured by Panamanian assets or definitively connected to Panamanian business is subject to a 6% statutory withholding rate, generally reduced to 5% under most Panama DTAs; interest on foreign-loan arrangements executed and payable abroad without Panamanian nexus may fall outside the territorial tax net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD (Panama Balboa pegged 1:1 to USD). Under Articles 762-A to 762-K of the Código Fiscal (introduced by Law 52 of 2019 and regulated by Executive Decree No. 717 of 2019), a taxpayer must file Form 078 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) and prepare a Local File when annual gross revenue exceeds USD 2,000,000 or when related-party transactions in the fiscal year exceed USD 250,000. A Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds USD 50,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting obligations apply only to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000 under Law 365 of 2024; standalone PIFs are exempt unless consolidated within a large MNE group.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply the Caribbean/UAE-style numbered Economic Substance Regulations, but the DGI enforces a substantive 'substance-over-form' doctrine rooted in Articles 697 and 698 of the Código Fiscal and reinforced by general anti-abuse rules in Law 365 of 2024. A PIF claiming territorial-source exclusion for SaaS revenue must demonstrate real and continuous commercial substance in Panama: a dedicated office or registered operational base, employed payroll and HR personnel, board decisions documented in Panama, active contracts with foreign clients, and actual performance of software engineering, licensing, and support functions. Without this, the DGI may recharacterize the PIF as a sham conduit, attribute its income to the foreign beneficial owner under source rules, and apply transfer pricing penalties. For PIFs deemed to carry on qualifying intellectual-property income activities, an organic DEMPE (Development, Enhancement, Maintenance, Protection, Exploitation) analysis must evidence that strategic decisions and core functions occur in Panama rather than in zero-tax offshore havens.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Under-Reporting (Defraudación Fiscal)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or false declaration of Panamanian-source income; mischaracterizing local SaaS payroll revenue as foreign-source; fabrication of deductible expenses; use of dual sets of books or shell invoices to artificially eliminate taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax plus monthly interest of 1%; closure of the establishment and suspension of the Aviso de Operación; criminal tax fraud under the reformed Código Fiscal carries imprisonment of 3 to 6 years and fines of up to USD 1,000,000 for amounts exceeding USD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and the resident agent are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency when they knowingly sign false returns or order fraudulent distributions; courts may pierce the PIF veil, order civil restitution of diverted profits, issue asset freezes and travel bans (impedimento de salida), and impose custodial sentences on de facto managers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a bare invoicing vehicle with no physical presence in Panama, no employees, no board meetings, and no software development or client-support function while attributing high-margin SaaS revenue to Panama to exploit the territorial tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI disregard of the foundation as a sham, causing all attributed income to be reclassified as Panamanian-source in the hands of the foreign beneficial owner; assessment of 25% ISR, 10% dividend tax, 100% evasion surcharge, monthly interest, and revocation of tax-exempt treatment; possible inclusion in public registries of non-cooperative taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors or council members who facilitate sham arrangements face personal liability for resulting taxes and penalties; under general commercial fraud doctrines they may be ordered to personally restore amounts distributed, prohibited from leaving Panama, and criminally prosecuted for conspiracy to defraud the Dirección General de Ingresos.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBI) Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or inaccurately filing the ultimate beneficial owner disclosure in Panama's Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (Law 23 of 2015 and implementing decrees); concealment of the founder or beneficiaries; accepting client funds derived from payroll fraud or bribery; processing payments through the PIF without KYC/CDD controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation for registry and AML failures; freezing of foundation assets; cancellation of the foundation's registration; money laundering predicate conviction under Law 23 of 2015 carries imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and fines of up to three times the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members, the resident agent, and the compliance officer are personally exposed to criminal liability for laundering and registry violations; sanctions include property confiscation, disqualification from acting as officers in Panama, travel restrictions, and extradition exposure under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., royalty payments to a foreign IP-holding affiliate, intercompany management fees, or payments to a foreign software development affiliate) executed without an arm's length benchmark, without Form 078, or without the required Local File / Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment of the transaction to the arm's length result, imposition of a penalty of up to 100% of the underpaid tax, monthly interest at 1%, and fixed fines for documentary non-compliance of up to USD 10,000 per infraction; repeated violations may suspend the taxpayer's Paz y Salvo status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who sign intercompany agreements and materially participate in pricing determinations without substantiation can be held jointly liable for the adjusted tax; the foundation's assets and the personal assets of the controlling council members are reachable where transfer pricing manipulation is found to be fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Compliance Failure (Dividends, Royalties, Interest)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to beneficiaries or paying royalties, interest, or technical service fees to non-residents without applying the statutory 10% dividend tax, 12.5% royalty tax, or 6% interest tax, and without verifying treaty relief conditions or the recipient's tax residence certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PIF as withholding agent is personally liable for 100% of the unwithheld tax plus a fine of 50% to 100% of that amount and monthly interest of 1%; third-party beneficiaries who knew of the omission are jointly liable for restitution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members who authorize distributions or cross-border payments without the appropriate withholding expose their personal assets to collection; deliberate and repeated non-withholding is treated as fraud and may result in criminal prosecution, travel bans, and disqualification of the resident agent.
